subject: AP Biology
stem: Researchers study how cell type X signals to target cells T in culture. (1) When X cells are mixed with T cells and touch them, T cells turn on gene Y. (2) When medium in which X cells grew for 24 hours is added to a separate dish of T cells, gene Y stays off. (3) When X and T cells share a dish but are separated by a porous membrane that lets proteins pass but prevents cell contact, gene Y stays off. (4) When T cells are treated with an antibody that blocks their receptor, touching X cells no longer turns on gene Y. Which best classifies the signaling from X to T?

choices.t: Contact-dependent (juxtacrine) signaling, because a signal on the surface of X binds the receptor on T only when the cells touch.
Paracrine signaling, because X releases a diffusible signal that acts on nearby T cells.
Endocrine signaling, because X releases a signal that travels through the fluid to distant T cells.
Autocrine signaling, because X cells respond to a signal they make themselves.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a developing tissue, a small group of cells secretes protein P. Cells within about 100 µm of the group turn on gene G, including cells that do not touch the group. Cells farther than 200 µm away do not respond. Protein P is broken down by enzymes in the extracellular fluid within minutes. When the group of cells is transplanted to a new site, cells within 100 µm of the graft turn on gene G. Which best classifies this signaling?

choices.t: Endocrine signaling, because a secreted protein travels to target cells in other parts of the body.
Paracrine signaling, because a short-lived secreted signal acts only on nearby cells.
Contact-dependent signaling, because the responding cells must be in direct membrane contact with the group.
Autocrine signaling, because the cells that secrete P are the ones that respond to it.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A tumor cell line makes growth factor G and has receptors for it. Single cells plated one per well, far from any other cell, still divide in medium with no added growth factor. Adding an antibody that binds and neutralizes G to the medium stops their division, and so does an antibody that blocks the G receptor. Which best classifies the signaling that drives division in these cells?

choices.t: Paracrine signaling, because G acts on nearby cells.
Autocrine signaling, because the cell makes a signal that binds its own receptors.
Contact-dependent signaling, because G is attached to the membrane of the neighboring cell.
Endocrine signaling, because G is carried through fluid to target cells.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A gland is removed from a rat, and the rat's liver cells stop breaking down glycogen. When a piece of the gland is transplanted under the skin of the ear, 20 cm from the liver, glycogen breakdown resumes. Skin cells next to the graft, which lack the receptor for the gland's hormone, show no response. Which statement best explains these results?

choices.t: The hormone acts as an autocrine signal, so only the gland cells in the graft respond to it.
The hormone acts as a paracrine signal, so the response depends on how close the target cells are to the graft.
The hormone acts as an endocrine signal: it travels in the blood to distant cells, and only cells with the receptor respond.
The hormone acts through direct cell-to-cell contact, so the graft must have grown into the liver.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
Ligand L binds a single receptor protein, R, which an antibody test shows is present on the surface of cell types 1, 2 and 4. Cell type 3 does not make R. A researcher adds L at the same concentration to each type.
Cell type | Labeled L bound | Response to L
1 | high | breaks down glycogen
2 | high | opens an ion channel
3 | none | none
4 | high | none
Which conclusion is best supported by all four rows?

choices.t: The structure of L alone determines the response, so L should cause the same response in every cell that binds it.
Binding to R is necessary but not sufficient: the response depends on the transduction proteins and effectors each cell type has, so the same ligand and receptor can give different responses or none.
Cell type 4 must lack receptor R, because a cell that binds a ligand but does not respond has no receptor.
Cell types 1 and 2 must have different receptors for L, because they respond to L in different ways.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A researcher engineers three cell lines to make the same receptor protein, R, at the same level. Each line is exposed to the same concentration of ligand L.
Cell line | Origin | Response to L
1 | liver | breaks down glycogen
2 | neuron | opens an ion channel
3 | skin fibroblast | begins dividing
Which statement best explains why one ligand and one receptor produce three responses?

choices.t: L enters each cell and decides which genes to turn on, because the response depends on the structure of the ligand.
The receptor R changes its structure in each cell line so that it binds a different part of L.
The cells differ in the number of L molecules that reached them, since only the amount of ligand determines the type of response.
Each cell line has its own set of signal transduction proteins and effectors, so the same receptor activation leads to different responses.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Cell line K binds labeled ligand L as strongly as a normal cell line does, yet shows no response. K lacks protein P, a cytoplasmic kinase that normally acts after receptor activation. When the gene for P is added to K, the cells respond to L. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: P is the receptor for L, because the response appeared only after P was supplied.
The receptor in K works, but the cells lacked a downstream component, P, needed to relay the signal to a response.
K could not bind L, so the original lack of response was caused by missing ligand binding.
P makes the ligand L, so adding P supplied the signal that K had been missing.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
Three cell lines were tested with ligand L. In a second test, a membrane-permeable drug that directly activates the downstream kinase of the pathway was added in place of L.
Cell line | Labeled L bound | Response to L | Response to the drug
1 | high | high | high
2 | none | none | high
3 | high | none | none
Which statement is best supported?

choices.t: Cell line 3 lacks the receptor, since it does not respond to L.
Cell line 2 lacks a functional receptor for L but has an intact downstream pathway, while cell line 3 has a receptor but a defect downstream.
Cell line 2 has a defect in transduction, since it gives no response to L.
Cell line 1 shows that receptors are never needed, since the drug alone can produce its response.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Ligand M is a 30-kDa protein. When M is added to the medium around liver cells, glycogen breakdown begins within 20 seconds. When M is microinjected directly into the cytoplasm of a liver cell, there is no response. The protein-synthesis inhibitor cycloheximide does not change the response to M added outside the cell, but a PKA inhibitor abolishes the response. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: M binds a receptor on the cell surface, and the response is relayed by proteins already in the cytoplasm, such as PKA, without new protein synthesis.
M enters the cell, binds an intracellular receptor, and acts as a transcription factor that produces new proteins within seconds.
M binds a membrane receptor, but the response needs newly synthesized proteins, and cycloheximide did not block them because it acts too slowly.
M enters the cell through a channel and directly activates PKA, which then breaks down glycogen.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Hormone S is a small nonpolar molecule. After S is added to cultured cells, the amount of a certain enzyme rises only after 3 hours. The transcription inhibitor actinomycin D prevents the rise. When S is attached to large beads that cannot cross the plasma membrane, there is no response. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: S binds a membrane receptor and activates a kinase cascade that acts within seconds.
S crosses the membrane and binds an intracellular receptor, and the complex changes gene expression, which explains the delay.
S acts at the cell surface, because the beads show that S can reach the cell from outside.
S must first be broken down in the cell to an active form, and transcription is not involved in the delay.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Neurotransmitter N is applied to a muscle fiber and depolarizes the membrane within 5 milliseconds. Replacing the Na⁺ outside the cell with a large ion that cannot pass through channels abolishes the depolarization. Kinase inhibitors and protein-synthesis inhibitors do not change the response. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: N crosses the membrane and binds an intracellular receptor that changes gene expression.
N binds a receptor that is itself an ion channel, so binding opens the channel and ions enter, with no second messenger or new gene expression needed.
N binds a receptor tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates transcription factors within milliseconds.
N causes IP₃ to release stored Ca²⁺ from the ER, and the Ca²⁺ then depolarizes the membrane.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a cell line, ligand L normally raises cAMP and turns on gene G. When drug Z is present, L no longer raises cAMP or turns on gene G, and binding of labeled L drops by 95%. In drug-treated cells, a membrane-permeable cAMP analog turns on gene G strongly. Which stage of signaling does Z most likely block?

choices.t: Transduction, because Z prevents the cell from making cAMP after L binds.
The response, because Z stops gene G from being turned on even when cAMP is high.
Reception, because Z stops L from binding its receptor, while transduction and the response are intact.
All three stages, because Z prevented L from turning on gene G.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a cell, each hormone-bound receptor activates 20 G proteins. Each active G protein activates one adenylyl cyclase, and each activated adenylyl cyclase makes 50 cAMP molecules before it is inactivated. A mutation lowers the number of G proteins activated per hormone-bound receptor from 20 to 5; all other steps are unchanged. If 300 receptors bind hormone, which statement describes the cAMP produced?

choices.t: 75,000 cAMP molecules, one fourth of the normal amount, because a smaller yield at the first step is carried through the later multiplying steps.
150,000 cAMP molecules, half of the normal amount, because the mutation removes half of the G proteins.
1,500 cAMP molecules, because only the 5 G proteins per receptor make cAMP.
300,000 cAMP molecules, unchanged, because the later steps of the cascade make up for the loss.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a kinase cascade, each active kinase K1 activates 10 molecules of K2, each active K2 activates 10 molecules of K3, and each active K3 phosphorylates 10 molecules of a transcription factor. A drug changes K2 so that each active K2 activates only 5 K3 molecules. If 40 K1 molecules are active, which statement describes the number of phosphorylated transcription factor molecules?

choices.t: 40,000, unchanged, because the later step adds 10 for each K3 and so corrects the loss.
10,000, one fourth of normal, because the change at the second step affects two steps.
200, because only the 5 K3 per K2 matter for the final amount.
20,000, half of the normal 40,000, because halving the output of one step halves the final output.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Two hypothetical pathways are compared. In pathway X, each of 100 ligand-bound receptors directly activates one transcription factor. In pathway Y, each of 100 ligand-bound receptors activates 5 kinase molecules, and each kinase activates 5 transcription factors. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Pathway Y activates 500 transcription factors, because each receptor activates 5 molecules.
Pathway Y activates 1,000 transcription factors, because the 5 and 5 are added at each receptor.
Pathway Y activates 2,500 transcription factors, which is 25 times as many as pathway X, because each step multiplies the signal.
Pathway X and Y activate the same number, because the number of receptors sets the number of active transcription factors.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A researcher measures how much of a cell's maximum response is produced when different fractions of its receptors are occupied by ligand.
Receptors occupied | Response (percent of maximum)
5% | 40%
20% | 85%
100% | 100%
Which interpretation is best supported by the data?

choices.t: The response is directly proportional to the fraction of receptors occupied, so 5% occupancy gives 5% of the maximum.
Occupancy above 20% harms the cell, so the response levels off.
Occupying a small fraction of the receptors gives a large share of the maximum response, as expected when downstream steps amplify the signal.
The ligand must enter the cell to produce a response, so the limit on the response is how fast the ligand is transported.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a signaling pathway, growth factor binding activates receptor R, which activates Ras, then Raf, then MEK, then ERK. Active ERK turns on genes for cell proliferation. A cell line has a mutation that keeps Raf active even without input from Ras. The cells are grown with no growth factor. Which result is predicted?

choices.t: The proliferation genes are on, and a MEK inhibitor turns them off, but an antibody that blocks receptor R does not.
The proliferation genes stay off until growth factor is added, because Raf cannot act without Ras.
The proliferation genes are on, and an antibody that blocks receptor R turns them off.
The proliferation genes are on, and a MEK inhibitor does not turn them off, because active Raf can bypass MEK.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In intestinal cells, a hormone binds a receptor that activates Gs, which activates adenylyl cyclase to make cAMP. cAMP activates PKA, and PKA triggers chloride secretion. Cholera toxin modifies Gs so that it cannot break down its bound GTP and stays active. Cells are treated with the toxin and no hormone. Which result is predicted?

choices.t: cAMP stays high, and a receptor antagonist lowers it, because the receptor must keep activating Gs.
cAMP stays low until the hormone is added, because Gs cannot work without the receptor.
cAMP stays high, but a PKA inhibitor has no effect on secretion, because cAMP acts independently of PKA.
cAMP stays high and chloride secretion continues, a receptor antagonist does not reduce it, and a PKA inhibitor does.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a pathway, ligand L activates receptor R. R activates kinase K1, and K1's only target is kinase K2. K2 phosphorylates transcription factor TF, which turns on gene G. A cell line has no functional K2 enzyme (the K2 protein is made but has no catalytic activity). Cells are treated with L. Which result is predicted?

choices.t: R is not activated, because the cell detects the missing K2 and blocks the receptor.
K1 is not activated either, because the pathway shuts off all steps when one step fails.
R and K1 are activated as usual, but TF is not phosphorylated and gene G stays off.
Gene G turns on at the normal level, because K1 can phosphorylate TF directly.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A receptor tyrosine kinase is normally activated when ligand binding makes two receptor molecules pair and phosphorylate each other, which then switches on a downstream kinase pathway. A cell line has a mutation that makes receptor molecules pair with each other even when no ligand is bound. Which result is predicted?

choices.t: The pathway is on without ligand, an inhibitor that blocks ligand binding has no effect, and an inhibitor of the receptor's kinase domain turns it off.
The downstream pathway stays off until ligand is added, because the receptors need ligand for any activity.
The pathway is on only briefly, because unpaired receptors quickly return to the ligand-bound form.
The pathway is on, and an inhibitor that blocks ligand binding turns it off.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
Three proteins, X, Y and Z, act in a single linear pathway between a receptor and a gene response. Researchers made cell lines that each lack one protein, then tested whether adding a constitutively active form of another protein (CA) turns on the response when no ligand is present.
Cell line | Response to ligand | CA-X, no ligand | CA-Y, no ligand | CA-Z, no ligand
Lacks X | none | not tested | response | no response
Lacks Y | none | no response | not tested | no response
Lacks Z | none | response | response | not tested
Which order of action, from the receptor to the response, fits the data?

choices.t: X, then Y, then Z.
Z, then Y, then X.
Y, then X, then Z.
Z, then X, then Y.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A pathway in a cell has three kinases, KA, KB and KC. After the ligand is added, the researchers add a drug that blocks one kinase at a time and measure which kinases become phosphorylated (active).
Drug target | KA phosphorylated | KB phosphorylated | KC phosphorylated
KA blocked | no | no | no
KB blocked | yes | no | no
KC blocked | yes | yes | no
Which order of action fits the data?

choices.t: KC, then KB, then KA.
KB, then KA, then KC.
The three kinases act in parallel, each one switched on directly by the receptor.
KA, then KB, then KC.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
Four proteins, F, G, H and J, act in a linear pathway from a receptor to a gene response. Each cell line lacks one protein. In each line, no ligand is given and a constitutively active form of one of the other proteins is added.
Cell line | Active forms that turn on the response
Lacks F | H, J, G
Lacks G | none
Lacks H | J, G
Lacks J | G
Which order of action, from the receptor to the response, fits the data?

choices.t: J, then H, then F, then G.
G, then J, then H, then F.
F, then H, then J, then G.
F, then J, then H, then G.

subject: AP Biology
stem: After a hormone is added to cells, three proteins, T, S and U, become phosphorylated: T at 10 seconds, S at 30 seconds, and U at 60 seconds. When an inhibitor of T is added before the hormone, neither S nor U is phosphorylated. When an inhibitor of U is added before the hormone, T and S are still phosphorylated. Which order of action fits the data?

choices.t: U, then S, then T.
S, then T, then U.
T, then S, then U.
T and U act separately, and S acts after both.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In healthy people, the pituitary hormone ACTH stimulates the adrenal cortex to release cortisol, and cortisol acts on the hypothalamus and pituitary to reduce ACTH release. A patient takes a drug that blocks an enzyme the adrenal cortex needs to make cortisol. The adrenal cortex and pituitary otherwise work normally. Which pattern of blood hormone levels is expected after two weeks?

choices.t: Cortisol low and ACTH high, because less cortisol means less inhibition of ACTH release.
Cortisol low and ACTH low, because low cortisol reduces the stimulus for ACTH release.
Cortisol low and ACTH normal, because cortisol does not regulate ACTH release.
Cortisol normal and ACTH normal, because negative feedback always returns hormone levels to normal whatever the drug.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A patient takes a high dose of prednisone, a drug that acts like cortisol, for several months. Normally, ACTH from the pituitary stimulates the adrenal cortex to make cortisol, and cortisol reduces ACTH release. Which change in the patient's own ACTH release and adrenal cortex is expected?

choices.t: ACTH release rises and the adrenal cortex enlarges, because the body needs to make more cortisol.
ACTH release is unchanged and the adrenal cortex is unchanged, because a drug cannot affect the loop.
ACTH release falls and the adrenal cortex enlarges, because less ACTH makes the adrenal cortex grow.
ACTH release falls and the adrenal cortex shrinks, because the drug acts like cortisol and the adrenal cortex gets less stimulation.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Parathyroid cells release PTH when blood Ca²⁺ is low. PTH raises blood Ca²⁺. A calcium-sensing receptor on parathyroid cells detects high blood Ca²⁺ and reduces PTH release. A patient has a mutation that makes the receptor insensitive to Ca²⁺. Which pattern is expected?

choices.t: PTH low and blood Ca²⁺ low, because the cells cannot sense calcium.
PTH high and blood Ca²⁺ high, because the cells do not detect high Ca²⁺ and keep releasing PTH.
PTH normal and blood Ca²⁺ normal, because other organs make up for the missing sensor.
PTH high and blood Ca²⁺ low, because the cells release PTH but it cannot act.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a bacterium, enzyme 1 begins a pathway that makes end product Z. Z normally binds an allosteric site on enzyme 1 and inhibits it. A mutant enzyme 1 has a normal active site but can no longer bind Z. Compared with the normal bacterium, which result is expected?

choices.t: Z levels are lower in the mutant, because the mutant enzyme has lost activity.
Z levels are the same, because the cell breaks down any extra Z.
Z levels are lower in the mutant, because the loss of feedback inhibition acts as positive feedback.
Z levels are higher in the mutant, because enzyme 1 stays active when Z accumulates.

subject: AP Biology
stem: During labor, the baby's head presses on the cervix, stretch receptors signal the hypothalamus, and the posterior pituitary releases oxytocin. Oxytocin makes the uterine muscle contract more strongly, which presses the head harder on the cervix. After delivery the cervix is no longer stretched and oxytocin release falls. A student claims: "This is negative feedback, because the process stops by itself at the end." Which evaluation is best?

choices.t: The claim is wrong: the contractions increase the stimulus that raises oxytocin, which is positive feedback, and the loop ends only because delivery removes the stimulus.
The claim is correct, because any process that ends on its own is negative feedback.
The claim is wrong, because hormones can take part only in positive feedback loops.
The claim is correct, because negative feedback means the response is helpful to the organism.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a neuron, depolarization opens voltage-gated Na⁺ channels, Na⁺ entry depolarizes the membrane further, and that opens more Na⁺ channels. Within about a millisecond, the channels inactivate and K⁺ channels open, which returns the membrane toward its resting value. A student claims: "Cells must keep conditions steady, so a positive feedback loop cannot occur inside a cell." Which evaluation is best?

choices.t: The claim is correct, because positive feedback always damages cells.
The claim is wrong: the opening of Na⁺ channels is positive feedback that rapidly amplifies the depolarization, and it is brief and is ended by channel inactivation.
The claim is correct, because the Na⁺ channel step must be negative feedback, since the membrane returns to rest.
The claim is wrong, because Na⁺ channel opening is negative feedback that keeps the membrane near its set point.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A ripening apple releases ethylene gas. Ethylene triggers cells in the apple, and in nearby apples, to make more ethylene, so the ethylene concentration rises rapidly. A student claims: "A feedback loop must keep a variable steady, so this cannot be a feedback loop at all." Which evaluation is best?

choices.t: The claim is correct, because ethylene production keeps changing and so there is no feedback.
The claim is correct, because only negative feedback loops count as feedback.
The claim is wrong, because this is negative feedback with a set point at a very high ethylene level.
The claim is wrong: this is a positive feedback loop, in which the output increases the stimulus and drives the variable further from its starting value.

subject: AP Biology
stem: When body temperature rises above 37°C, the sweat rate increases. As the sweat evaporates, body temperature falls back toward 37°C and the sweat rate decreases. A student claims: "This is positive feedback, because sweat rate went up when the temperature went up." Which evaluation is best?

choices.t: The claim is correct, because the response and the stimulus changed in the same direction.
The claim is correct, because sweating is an amplified response.
The claim is wrong: sweating opposes the rise in temperature and returns it toward the set point, which is negative feedback.
The claim is wrong, because feedback loops involve hormones and sweating is controlled by nerves.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A researcher examines 200 cells from a growing root tip under the microscope. The cell cycle in this tissue lasts 24 hours. Counts: interphase 160, prophase 16, metaphase 8, anaphase 6, telophase 10. About how long does a cell spend in metaphase?

choices.t: About 0.04 hours, because 8 of 200 cells are in metaphase.
About 1.9 hours, because 8 of every 100 cells are in metaphase.
About 4.8 hours, because 8 of the 40 dividing cells are in metaphase.
About 1.0 hour, because 8/200 of the cells are in metaphase and the cycle is 24 hours long.

subject: AP Biology
stem: An onion root tip sample of 300 cells is counted. The cell cycle lasts 20 hours. Counts: interphase 240, prophase 30, metaphase 12, anaphase 6, telophase 12. About how long does a cell spend in mitosis (prophase through telophase)?

choices.t: About 0.2 hours, because 60 of 300 cells are in mitosis.
About 5 hours, because 60 cells in mitosis divided by 240 cells in interphase is 25% of 20 hours.
About 4 hours, because 60 of the 300 cells are in mitosis, which is 20% of the 20-hour cycle.
About 16 hours, because most of the cells are in the stage with no visible chromosomes.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a culture of dividing cells, 5% of the cells are in metaphase at any moment, and metaphase lasts 30 minutes. What is the length of the whole cell cycle?

choices.t: 2.5 hours, because 0.5 hours is multiplied by 5.
0.025 hours, because 0.5 hours is multiplied by 0.05.
9.5 hours, because the 0.5 hours of metaphase is subtracted from the 10-hour cycle.
10 hours, because 0.5 hours is 5% of the cycle length.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A researcher counts 200 cells from a culture before and after 6 hours of treatment with a drug.
Phase | Before drug | After 6 hours of drug
Interphase | 190 | 70
Prophase | 4 | 8
Metaphase | 3 | 118
Anaphase | 1 | 1
Telophase | 2 | 3
Which interpretation is best supported?

choices.t: The drug speeds up mitosis, because far more cells are in mitosis after treatment.
The drug blocks the move from metaphase to anaphase, so cells that enter mitosis pile up in metaphase.
The drug stops cells from entering mitosis, because the number of interphase cells fell.
The drug blocks cytokinesis, because cells accumulate at the end of mitosis.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A cultured cell line has 3.0 pg of DNA per cell in G1 and 6.0 pg after DNA replication is complete, until the cell divides. Flow cytometry measures DNA per cell.
Sample | Cells at 3.0 pg | Cells between 3.0 and 6.0 pg | Cells at 6.0 pg
Untreated | 52% | 18% | 30%
24 hours with drug D | 6% | 9% | 85%
Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: Drug D arrests cells in G1, before DNA replication begins.
Drug D arrests cells during S phase, partway through DNA replication.
Drug D lets cells replicate their DNA but arrests them in G2 or mitosis, before the cell divides.
Drug D makes cells leave the cycle and enter G0, in which they hold 6.0 pg of DNA.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A haploid yeast strain has a temperature-sensitive mutation in a gene. DNA content is measured in relative units (1 unit in G1, 2 units after replication).
Sample | Cells at 1 unit | Cells between 1 and 2 units | Cells at 2 units
Permissive temperature | 50% | 20% | 30%
4 hours at restrictive temperature | 92% | 5% | 3%
Which conclusion is best supported about the mutated gene?

choices.t: The gene product is needed to move from G1 into DNA replication.
The gene product is needed to complete DNA replication during S phase.
The gene product is needed to carry out mitosis, so cells pile up with replicated DNA.
The gene product is needed for cytokinesis, so cells pile up with two nuclei and 2 units of DNA.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A drug that blocks nucleotide synthesis is added to cultured cells that hold 3.0 pg of DNA in G1 and 6.0 pg after replication. After 12 hours, flow cytometry shows 8% of cells at 3.0 pg, 87% between 3.0 and 6.0 pg, and 5% at 6.0 pg. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: DNA replication began but cannot be completed, so most cells are stuck partway through S phase.
The cells are arrested in G1, before replication starts.
The cells are arrested in G2, after replication is complete.
The cells are arrested in mitosis, before the cells divide.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Cells are kept in medium without serum for 4 days. Flow cytometry shows 93% of the cells at 3.0 pg of DNA (the amount in G1 before replication). Twenty hours after serum is added, 40% of the cells are at 3.0 pg, 35% are between 3.0 and 6.0 pg, and 25% are at 6.0 pg. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: The starved cells were arrested before DNA replication (in G1 or G0), and serum let them re-enter the cycle, replicate DNA and move on.
The starved cells were arrested in G2, and serum made them divide and enter G1.
Serum blocks DNA replication, so the cells between 3.0 and 6.0 pg are damaged.
Serum makes cells skip S phase and go directly into mitosis.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In dividing cells, the concentration of the kinase CDK1 stays constant. Cyclin B accumulates during G2, peaks at metaphase, and falls sharply at anaphase. CDK1 kinase activity rises and falls with the amount of cyclin B. A mutant cyclin B cannot be degraded. Which outcome is most likely in cells that make only the mutant cyclin B?

choices.t: The cells never enter mitosis, because CDK1 cannot be activated by the mutant cyclin.
The cells enter mitosis normally but cannot complete it, because CDK1 activity stays high after anaphase.
The cells skip mitosis and begin another round of DNA replication, because cyclin B is present.
The cells divide normally, because the amount of CDK1 and not the amount of cyclin sets the timing.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
A researcher measures a cell population through one cell cycle.
Stage | CDK1 protein (relative) | Cyclin B (relative) | CDK1 kinase activity (relative)
G1 | 1.0 | 0.1 | 0.1
S | 1.0 | 0.2 | 0.2
G2 | 1.0 | 0.8 | 0.7
Metaphase | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0
After anaphase | 1.0 | 0.1 | 0.1
Which statement best explains why kinase activity changes even though the amount of CDK1 stays the same?

choices.t: CDK1 is active only when it is bound to cyclin B, so kinase activity follows the cyclin B level.
CDK1 is made and degraded in each cycle, so its amount follows the activity.
CDK1 activity is independent of cyclin B, and the matching pattern is a coincidence.
Cyclin B is an enzyme that phosphorylates targets by itself, and CDK1 only holds it in place.

subject: AP Biology
stem: After DNA damage, a cell makes large amounts of p21, a protein that binds and inhibits cyclin-CDK complexes needed to pass from G1 into S phase. Which result is predicted in the cells with high p21?

choices.t: CDK activity rises and the cells enter S phase faster.
CDK activity falls, and the cells arrest in G2 after DNA replication.
CDK activity falls, and the cells arrest in G1 before DNA replication begins.
CDK activity is unchanged, because inhibitors act only on cyclin synthesis.

subject: AP Biology
stem: In a classic experiment, researchers fused cells at different stages of the cell cycle. When a G1 cell was fused to a cell in S phase, the G1 nucleus began to replicate DNA early. When a G1 cell was fused to a cell in M phase, the G1 nucleus condensed its chromosomes. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: The cytoplasm of S-phase and M-phase cells contains diffusible regulators that can push a nucleus from G1 into that phase.
The stage of a cell is set only by the amount of DNA in its nucleus, with no role for cytoplasmic factors.
Regulators of the cell cycle stay inside the nucleus and cannot move between cells.
G1 nuclei hold inhibitors that stop S and M phase from starting.

subject: AP Biology
stem:
Cells with normal p53 (WT) and cells with a mutated p53 gene are grown, and half of each group is exposed to UV light that damages DNA. Twenty-four hours later, researchers measure the percent of cells in G1 and S and the level of p21 protein.
Cells | UV | In G1 | In S | p21 level
WT | no | 60% | 30% | low
WT | yes | 90% | 4% | high
Mutated p53 | no | 60% | 30% | low
Mutated p53 | yes | 58% | 31% | low
Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: p53 speeds up the cell cycle, because WT cells have more cells in G1.
The mutated cells are in G0 after UV exposure, because they show no change.
After DNA damage, p53 raises p21 and holds cells in G1; without p53, damaged cells continue into S phase.
p53 repairs the UV damage directly, which allows the WT cells to enter S phase.

subject: AP Biology
stem: The Rb protein binds the transcription factor E2F in G1 and prevents E2F from turning on S-phase genes. Growth factor signaling leads to phosphorylation of Rb, which releases E2F. A cell line has no functional Rb. The cells are grown without growth factor. Which result is predicted?

choices.t: S-phase genes stay off until growth factor is added, because E2F also needs the growth factor.
S-phase genes are off in these cells, because Rb is needed to make E2F.
The cells arrest in G2, because Rb acts only at the G2 checkpoint.
E2F is free and S-phase genes are expressed, so the cells can enter S phase without growth factor.

subject: AP Biology
stem: Normal fibroblasts (N) and tumor cells (T) are grown in culture. At low density they divide at the same rate. At high density, 95% of N cells are in G1 or G0 and stop dividing, but 30% of the T cells are still in S phase and the cells pile into layers. Adding 10 times more growth factor does not restart the N cells at high density. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: T cells divide faster than N cells at all densities.
N cells stop at high density because they ran out of growth factor.
T cells at high density are in G0, which lets them pile up.
T cells do not respond to the signals that normally stop the cycle at high density, while N cells do.

subject: AP Biology
stem: A drug that prevents spindle formation is added to cells. In normal cells, 85% stop with condensed chromosomes and no anaphase. In cells that lack Mad2, a spindle checkpoint protein, most cells leave mitosis within 1.5 hours with unaligned chromosomes and produce daughter cells with abnormal chromosome numbers. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.t: Mad2 is needed to condense chromosomes, because the cells lacking it have abnormal chromosome numbers.
The spindle checkpoint normally delays anaphase until the chromosomes are attached to the spindle, so cells without Mad2 divide with misaligned chromosomes.
Mad2 is needed to build the spindle, because the drug blocks spindle formation in the cells lacking Mad2.
Mad2 drives cells through anaphase, because cells without Mad2 leave mitosis more slowly.
